description:
By the winter of 1349, half the people of Europe were dead. Villages stood empty, wheat rotted in the fields, and the church bells rang for no one. This was the Black Death — the deadliest plague in human history.

Watch the full story on Echoes of History Channel.
label: Cold open: half of Europe dead + the question (loop: question -> answer)
title: Half of Europe Died in Just Six Years #shorts #history #documentary #foryou

description:
At the siege of Caffa in 1347, a dying khan ordered the bodies of his own dead loaded into catapults and hurled over the city walls. The plague was inside — and the merchants who fled by ship carried it home to Europe.

Watch the full story on Echoes of History Channel.
label: Death at Caffa: catapulted dead + merchants carry plague home (loop)
onscreen_text: THE DEAD RAINED OVER THE WALLS
title: They Catapulted the Dead Over the City Walls #shorts #history #documentary #foryou

description:
In October 1347, twelve galleys limped into Messina, Sicily — their crews dying where they stood. The people called them the death ships and drove them out with burning arrows. It was too late: the rats had already slipped ashore.

Watch the full story on Echoes of History Channel.
label: The Death Ships reach Messina, October 1347 (loop: rats ashore -> ships arrive)
title: The Death Ships That Doomed a Continent #shorts #history #documentary #foryou
